title.en: Axisymmetric equilibrium to solver-grid material support
title.zh: 轴对称平衡到求解网格材料支撑

summary: Reconstruct an axisymmetric equilibrium on a Cartesian solver grid and classify the material support of that grid, composing the mapping relation and the material-support relation in one ordered DAG with the retained entry's call shape.
aliases: coarse CAD grid material support composition

identity.relation: an axisymmetric equilibrium mapping and a Cartesian solver grid to the static field, the poloidal flux, the material support mask, and the mapping's coverage and clamping diagnostics
identity.direction: equilibrium, x_m, y_m, z_m, xpoint_half_length_m, pml_cells, pec_mask -> magnetic_flux_density_t, poloidal_flux_wb_per_rad, material_support_mask, covered_mask, radially_clamped_point_count, axially_clamped_point_count, closed_flux_mask, axis_segment_mask
identity.definition: Reconstructs the static field and the poloidal flux on the solver grid, builds the cylindrical coordinates of that grid, reads the separatrix flux and the selected flux-surface side off the caller's equilibrium mapping, and classifies material support from the reconstructed flux and those parameters.
identity.model: the composed tensor-product equilibrium reconstruction followed by the geometric material-support classification; no field solve is performed
identity.geometry: axisymmetric R-Z equilibrium map evaluated on a rectilinear Cartesian solver grid, then classified in the solver box
identity.coordinates: cylindrical for the map, Cartesian for the grid, with the axial coordinate shared between them
identity.boundary: the composition's boundary is the union of its two dependency boundaries: query points outside the map box are clamped and reported, and the support mask must be non-empty or the call fails
assumptions: The equilibrium mapping carries both the map arrays and the flux-surface classification parameters, which is the retained entry's own layout.
The grid axes are shared between the mapping relation and the coordinate glue, so both agree about the solver box.
The composition is a pure ordered DAG: it has no feedback loop, no iteration, and no state between calls.
The caller owns every array; the graph returns views of the dependencies' own results without copying them.

inputs.name: equilibrium
inputs.description: Caller-owned equilibrium mapping carrying the map arrays r_m, z_m, psi_wb_per_rad, br_t, bz_t and the classification parameters separatrix_flux_wb_per_rad and closed_flux_side.
inputs.constraints: Must be a mapping. The map arrays must satisfy the mapping relation's contract; the two classification parameters must satisfy the material-support relation's contract.

inputs.name: x_m
inputs.constraints: Finite, one-dimensional, at least two points, strictly increasing.

inputs.name: y_m
inputs.constraints: Finite, one-dimensional, at least two points, strictly increasing.

inputs.name: z_m
inputs.constraints: Finite, one-dimensional, at least two points, strictly increasing.

inputs.name: xpoint_half_length_m
inputs.description: Poloidal half length passed to the material-support relation.

inputs.name: pml_cells
inputs.description: PML frame thickness passed to the material-support relation.

inputs.name: pec_mask
inputs.description: Caller-owned PEC mask passed to the material-support relation.
inputs.constraints: Must match the solver grid shape.

outputs.name: magnetic_flux_density_t
outputs.description: Static magnetic field on the solver grid.
outputs.constraints: Finite everywhere; the transverse pair is exactly zero on the grid axis.

outputs.name: poloidal_flux_wb_per_rad
outputs.description: Poloidal flux per radian interpolated onto the solver grid.
outputs.constraints: Finite everywhere, evaluated at the clamped query coordinates.

outputs.name: material_support_mask
outputs.description: Grid points carrying cold-plasma material support.
outputs.constraints: Guaranteed non-empty; an empty classification fails the call.

outputs.name: covered_mask
outputs.description: Grid points that lay inside the closed box spanned by the map axes.
outputs.constraints: Produced by the mapping relation and passed through unchanged.

outputs.name: radially_clamped_point_count
outputs.description: Grid points whose radius exceeded the outer map radius.
outputs.constraints: Produced by the mapping relation and passed through unchanged.

outputs.name: axially_clamped_point_count
outputs.description: Grid points clamped onto an axial map face.
outputs.constraints: Produced by the mapping relation and passed through unchanged.

outputs.name: closed_flux_mask
outputs.description: Covered grid points on the selected side of the separatrix flux, before the frame and conductor exclusions.
outputs.constraints: An added diagnostic output; it is a subset of covered_mask and is what lets a caller attribute an empty support mask to the flux-surface choice.

outputs.name: axis_segment_mask
outputs.description: Covered grid points at the grid's innermost radius within the poloidal half length, before the frame and conductor exclusions.
outputs.constraints: An added diagnostic output; it is empty whenever the equilibrium map's radial axis begins above the grid's minimum radius.

preconditions: The caller's equilibrium mapping carries both the map arrays and the two flux-surface classification parameters, as the retained entry expected.
Both bound relations' preconditions hold for the supplied arrays.
The solver box has a genuine PML frame of at least one cell.
supported: Any rectilinear Cartesian solver grid and any axisymmetric equilibrium map satisfying the two dependency contracts.
Either separatrix side, and any positive PML frame thickness that leaves a non-empty interior.
Both dependencies being replaced by caller-supplied callables with the same contracts.
excluded: Field solves, wave propagation, and plasma response.
Solver grids without a PML frame.
Any graph-level iteration, feedback, or state; this composition is a single ordered pass.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError when inputs is not a mapping, when any of the seven required inputs is missing, when equilibrium is not a mapping, or when the equilibrium mapping does not carry the two classification parameters. Validation failures of either bound relation propagate unchanged, so the failing parameter is named by the relation that owns it.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: A dependency failure aborts the graph and propagates; no fallback implementation is selected and no retry is attempted.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; this TaskGraph is an ordered DAG with no feedback loop.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial result is returned after a node failure.

provenance.lineage_summary: SciRel-owned composition replacing the single retained coarse-CAD operator with its two independent scientific identities plus an explicit ordered DAG. The retained entry owned the cylindrical-to-Cartesian reconstruction and the material-support classification inside one callable; the review found that the two share no scientific input, so they are proposed as separately reviewable assets and this graph is the composition that reproduces the retained call shape, the retained output names and shapes, and the retained results exactly. The graph adds the closed-flux and innermost-radius masks as diagnostics so that an expert can attribute a surprising support mask, and it takes the retained zero-thickness PML defect's explicit precondition from the classification relation rather than re-deriving it. The observation snapshot and the batch inventory are private review artifacts and are not part of the public contract.

example.description: Compose both relations on a synthetic equilibrium and a 9x9x7 solver grid, and check that the six retained outputs are present with their retained shapes.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.geometry import solve_axisymmetric_equilibrium_grid_mapping
r_axis = np.linspace(0.05, 1.0, 21)
z_axis = np.linspace(-0.5, 0.5, 21)
rr, zz = np.meshgrid(r_axis, z_axis, indexing='ij')
equilibrium = {
    'r_m': r_axis,
    'z_m': z_axis,
    'psi_wb_per_rad': 0.9 * rr + 0.1 * np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * zz),
    'br_t': 0.3 * rr - 0.1 * zz ** 2,
    'bz_t': 1.0 - 0.4 * rr ** 2,
    'separatrix_flux_wb_per_rad': 0.4,
    'closed_flux_side': 'less_than',
}
result = solve_axisymmetric_equilibrium_grid_mapping(inputs={
    'equilibrium': equilibrium,
    'x_m': np.linspace(-0.5, 0.5, 9),
    'y_m': np.linspace(-0.5, 0.5, 9),
    'z_m': np.linspace(-0.4, 0.4, 7),
    'xpoint_half_length_m': 0.2,
    'pml_cells': 1,
    'pec_mask': np.zeros((9, 9, 7), dtype=bool),
})
assert result['magnetic_flux_density_t'].shape == (9, 9, 7, 3)
assert result['poloidal_flux_wb_per_rad'].shape == (9, 9, 7)
assert result['covered_mask'].sum() == 560
assert result['material_support_mask'].sum() > 0
assert result['closed_flux_mask'].sum() >= result['material_support_mask'].sum()
assert result['axis_segment_mask'].sum() == 0
assert result['radially_clamped_point_count'] == 0
assert result['axially_clamped_point_count'] == 0
assert not result['material_support_mask'][0, :, :].any()
assert not result['material_support_mask'][:, :, -1].any()
example.expected: A finite static field and poloidal flux on the 9x9x7 grid, 560 covered points, a non-empty support mask with nothing on the solver-box faces, and an empty innermost-radius segment.

scope: Exact agreement of the six retained outputs with the retained single operator on the same inputs.
Binding of exactly the two declared dependencies, verified by injected recording callables.
Rejection of unknown composition keywords and of a missing required input.
The graph's imports, and the absence of any file, YAML, or source-checkout read at run time.
The declared dependency closure against the graph's own nodes, and the connectivity of every declared input and output.
Forwarding of the classification parameters from the equilibrium mapping verbatim, verified by moving the support mask while the mapping outputs stay fixed.
Agreement between the coordinate glue and the mapping relation's own coverage mask.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Establishes that the composition reproduces the retained entry and that its declared dependency closure, connectivity, and purity hold. It does not establish that either dependency is physically adequate for a device, and it does not establish the composition's suitability for grids or equilibria outside the tested contracts.
known_limitations: The composition inherits both dependencies' limitations, including the clamped out-of-box policy and the innermost-radius proxy for the magnetic axis.
The two added diagnostic masks are not part of the retained output set, so a caller that compares output key sets against the retained entry must account for them.
The graph has no feedback loop by design, so an equilibrium that would need to be re-derived from the reconstructed field is out of scope.
Public distribution licensing remains pending a human decision.

nodes.description: Validate the three caller-owned grid axes and build the radius and axial coordinate of every grid point.
Reconstruct the static field and poloidal flux on the solver grid and report coverage and clamping.
Read the separatrix flux and the selected flux-surface side off the caller's equilibrium mapping.
Classify material support from the reconstructed flux, the grid coordinates, and the caller's frame and conductor declarations.

execution.ordering: Validate the caller's declarations, reconstruct the static field and poloidal flux on the solver grid, build the cylindrical coordinates of that grid, read the classification parameters off the equilibrium mapping, classify material support from the reconstructed flux and those parameters, and return.
execution.state_ownership: The caller owns the equilibrium mapping, the grid axes, the PEC mask, and every returned array; the graph owns only the two coordinate arrays it builds for the current call and retains no mutable state between calls.
execution.failure_propagation: Validation or dependency failure aborts the call immediately; no fallback, retry, or partial result is produced.
